title: Find the Count of Monotonic Pairs II
notes:
## Intuition

Once `arr1` is chosen, `arr2` is forced (`arr2[i] = nums[i] - arr1[i]`), so we only count valid `arr1` arrays. Trying every array is exponential, but the only thing the next position cares about is the current value of `arr1`. That gives a DP over (position, value of `arr1[i]`).

Going from value `k` at `i - 1` to value `j` at `i` needs `k <= j` (for `arr1`) and `nums[i - 1] - k >= nums[i] - j` (for `arr2`). Together: `k <= j - shift` with `shift = max(0, nums[i] - nums[i - 1])`. So each new cell is a prefix sum of the old row.

## Approach

1. `dp[j]` counts valid prefixes ending with `arr1[i] = j`. At `i = 0` every `j` from 0 to `nums[0]` gives 1 way.
2. For each next index, compute `shift`, the minimum rise `arr1` must make.
3. Build `prefix` so that `prefix[k]` is the sum of `dp[0..k]`.
4. For each `j` from `shift` to `nums[i]`, set `next[j] = prefix[j - shift]`; smaller `j` has no valid predecessor.
5. Replace `dp` with `next`; at the end, sum `dp` modulo `10^9 + 7`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 3, 2]`. Start: `dp = [1, 1, 1, 0]`.

- `i = 1`: `shift = 1`, `prefix = [1, 2, 3, 3]`, so `next[1..3] = prefix[0..2]` and `dp = [0, 1, 2, 3]`.
- `i = 2`: `shift = 0`, `prefix = [0, 1, 3, 6]`, so `next[0..2] = [0, 1, 3]`.

The total is `0 + 1 + 3 = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · m), where m is the largest value: each index builds a prefix row and a new row of length m + 1.
- Space: O(m): only the current row, its prefix sums and the next row are kept.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the `arr2` side: the bound is `j - shift`, not just `j`.
- Starting the inner loop at 0 instead of `shift` would read a negative index.
- Summing over all pairs `(k, j)` directly costs O(n · m²), too slow for 2000 × 1000.
- Apply the modulus while building `prefix` and the final total.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MOD` | the modulus `10^9 + 7` |
| `maxValue` | largest value in `nums`, the row width |
| `dp` | ways for each value of `arr1` at the current index |
| `shift` | how much `arr1` must rise at index `i` |
| `prefix` | running sums of `dp` |
| `next` | the row for index `i` |
| `total` | the final count |

narration.3: The largest value bounds every possible arr1 entry, so it sets the row width.
narration.4: dp[j] will count the valid prefixes whose current arr1 value is j.
narration.5: At the first index arr1[0] can be any value from 0 to nums[0].
narration.6: Each of those starts exactly one valid prefix.
narration.8: Extend the prefixes one index at a time.
narration.9: If nums rises, arr2 can only stay level by arr1 rising at least that much, so shift is the minimum rise.
narration.11: Start the running sums of the previous row.
narration.12: Walk across the previous row once.
narration.13: prefix[k] is the number of prefixes whose last arr1 value is at most k.
narration.16: Only values of j at least shift can follow some earlier value.
narration.17: Every earlier value up to j - shift keeps both arrays monotonic, so add them all at once.
narration.19: The new row becomes the current row.
narration.22: After the last index, every value of arr1 ends some valid pair.
narration.23: Add its count to the answer, keeping it reduced.
narration.25: Return the number of monotonic pairs modulo 10^9 + 7.
